title: Gradient of a curve & area under a graph
examples: How do I find the gradient if I only have a graph?
Is the area under the curve always a trapezium?
What does the gradient mean when I am looking at speed versus time?

explain.say: Today we will learn to estimate gradients and areas.

draw.text: Gradient of a curve & area under a graph

explain.say: To estimate the gradient at one point, we use a tangent line.
We draw a straight line that touches the curve at that point.

draw.text: Draw a line touching the curve

explain.say: Then we pick two points on that straight line to calculate the gradient.

draw.text: Use two points on the tangent line

explain.say: For the area, we use trapeziums under the curve.

faq.q: Why do I use trapeziums for the area?
faq.a: Trapeziums are used because they give a good straight-line approximation for the curved area.
asks: What is the trapezium rule for area?
How do I approximate area with shapes?

faq.q: When do I use the tangent estimate?
faq.a: You use the tangent estimate when you need the instantaneous gradient at a single point.
asks: What is the gradient at a specific point?
When is a tangent line useful?

faq.q: What are the formula for the trapezium area?
faq.a: The area is found by averaging the parallel sides and multiplying by the perpendicular distance.
asks: How do I calculate the area using this method?

faq.q: Does the gradient mean anything in real life?
faq.a: Yes, if the graph is speed versus time, the gradient is the acceleration.
asks: What is the gradient in physics?
What does the slope represent here?

faq.q: Can I use rectangles instead of trapeziums?
faq.a: You can, but trapeziums are usually more accurate for curves because they account for the curve's shape better.
asks: Which shape is better for area estimation?

facts: The gradient measures the steepness of a line or curve.
The tangent line touches the curve at exactly one point.
The area under a curve is often estimated using trapeziums.
If the graph is distance versus time, the gradient is speed.

quiz.say: If a graph shows speed versus time, what does the gradient represent?
quiz.why: The gradient of speed versus time always gives the rate of change of speed, which is acceleration.

wrong.1: This is the value on the y-axis, not the rate of change.
wrong.2: Distance is related to the area under the graph, not the gradient.
wrong.3: Time is the variable on the x-axis, not the gradient itself.

quiz.say: To estimate the gradient at point P, what should you draw?

options.show: A secant line between two points
options.say: A secant line between two points

quiz.why: You must draw a tangent line that just touches the curve at the specific point P.

wrong.0: A vertical line has an undefined gradient, which is not helpful for estimation.
wrong.2: A secant line cuts through the curve at two points, not just touching one.
wrong.3: A horizontal line only gives a gradient of zero, which is usually incorrect.

quiz.say: Which method is best for estimating the area under a curve?
quiz.why: Trapeziums provide a much better approximation of the curve's area than simple rectangles.

wrong.1: Rectangles assume the curve is straight between the points, which is often not true.
wrong.2: Triangles only account for half the area, making the estimate too small.
wrong.3: This is for exact integration, not for estimation using shapes.
